fix(transport): replay seekable request bodies on retry

http.NewRequest only sets GetBody for the body types it recognizes, so a
request built from any other io.Reader was sent with GetBody nil and the
retry transport refused to replay it. Uploads streamed from an *os.File
therefore failed on the first 429 while every other call retried.

Seekable bodies now get a GetBody that rewinds to the offset the caller
handed the reader over at, plus the exact Content-Length that implies, so
nothing is buffered. Bodies that are also io.Closers are wrapped: these
methods take an io.Reader, so closing stays the caller's job, and closing
the file after the first attempt would break the replay. Bodies that
cannot be rewound are still sent once rather than replayed truncated.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" && git log --oneline -1

Both parts of the report are fixed on branch `fix/file-upload-retries`.

## What was wrong

I reproduced it first. `http.NewRequest` only populates `GetBody` for the three body types it recognizes (`*bytes.Buffer`, `*bytes.Reader`, `*strings.Reader`). `RawClient.Do` passes a caller's `io.Reader` straight through, so a streamed multipart body arrived at the retry transport with `GetBody == nil`. The transport computes `canReplayBody` from exactly that field and returns the response unretried — including on 429, regardless of `RetryAllMethods`. Measured before the fix:

| body | attempts on 429 |
|---|---|
| `*bytes.Buffer` multipart | 2 (retried) |
| `io.Pipe` streamed multipart | 1 |
| `*os.File` | 1 |

That's the "every other call retries fine" asymmetry: JSON calls encode to a `*bytes.Reader` and replay; hand-streamed uploads don't.

## The fixes

**1. Seekable bodies replay** (`pipedrive/requestbody.go`). Any body implementing `io.Seeker` — an `os.Open` file included — gets a `GetBody` that rewinds to the offset the caller handed it over at, plus the exact `Content-Length` (these requests previously went out chunked). Nothing is buffered, so large uploads keep streaming. This covers `Files.Add`, `Files.Update`, `Persons.AddPicture` and `Raw.Do`.

A body that genuinely can't rewind (an `io.Pipe`) is still sent once — replaying a drained reader would upload a truncated file. That case is now documented rather than silent.

**2. `Files.Upload`** (`pipedrive/v1/files.go`) takes a file name and a reader, mirroring `CallLogs.AddRecording`:

```go
file, err := client.Files.Upload(ctx, "contract.pdf", f, v1.WithFileDealID(v1.DealID(42)))
```

All seven association fields from the `addFile` spec have typed options, plus `WithFileFormValues` as an escape hatch. It encodes via the existing `internal/multipartbody` helper, so the body is a `*bytes.Reader` and retries work unconditionally.
